This claim petition is filed by the petitioners claiming compensation of .60,00,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for the death of Smt.T.Rathnamma, W/o.Late.T.Rajappa in a road traffic accident.

2. The petition averments in brief is that on 08.06.2022 at about 12.30 p.m., when deceased was standing by the side of the road, Opp to Sapthagiri Grameena Bank, Pathikonda Village on Bengaluru - Chennai NH Road, Gangavaram Mandal, a Maruti Swift Car bearing Regn.No.KA-05-ND-9589, driven by its driver at high speed in a rash and negligent manner, dashed to the divider and then to deceased.
Due to said accident, deceased sustained injuries and died on the spot.
Thereafter, deceased was shifted to Area Hospital, Palamaner, wherein postmortem was conducted and body was handed over to petitioners and performed funeral and obsequies ceremonies.
Prior to the accident, the deceased was hale and healthy and was doing Agriculturist and Coolie work and earning a sum of .25,000/- per month.
Due to the death of deceased, the petitioners have lost their bread earning member of the family and put to lot of mental agony.
The accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of car by its driver.

The respondent No.1 to 3, being the owners and insurer of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to Tummisi Gangulappa vs Kaju Eswara Raju on 10 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163952893/

sentences.text: 3. In pursuance of service of notice, though respondent No.1 & 2 appeared before the tribunal through their respective counsel, they have not filed written statement.
The respondent No.3 appeared before the tribunal through the counsel and filed the written statement.
4. In the Written Statement, the respondent No.3 has denied the contents of claim petition specifically and categorically.
The respondent No.3 also denied age, occupation and income of deceased as well as place, time and manner of accident.
Further the respondent No.3 contended that the petition filed by the petitioners is not maintainable either in law or on facts and same is liable to be dismissed.
Further the petition has been filed before this court on 01.07.2023 and alleged accident occurred on 08.06.2022 and thus, the petition is barred by Limitation Act.
As such petition is liable to be dismissed.

Further contended that this respondent has issued certificate of insurance under Policy bearing No.98000031210911285011 i.e., bundled motor policy in favour of the respondent No.1 for the period 09.03.2022 to 08.03.2023 in respect of car bearing Engine No.K12NP1180280 and Chassis No.MBHCZCB3SNB965774 and the liability, if any, is subject to the terms and conditions of policy.
Further contended that
as per the charge sheet filed police, the accused/driver of insured vehicle alleged to have involved in the accident has been charged U/s.304(A) of IPC and Sec.3 R/w.181 of M.V.Act.
Further the driver of alleged offending vehicle was not having driving license at the time of alleged accident.

The respondent No.1 has allowed a person who was not having valid and effective driving license to drive the same as on the date of alleged accident and as such, the respondent No.1 has violated the terms and conditions of policy.
Further there was no negligence on the part of driver of insured vehicle in issue as he was proceeding with due care and caution by following the traffic rules and regulations.

Further contended that the alleged accident occurred due to the sole negligence of deceased who being pedestrian crossing the national highway in a negligent manner without following traffic rules and regulations and caused the accident.
The amount claimed by petitioners is highly exorbitant.
Hence, prays to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of above pleadings, learned predecessor in office has framed the following:
ISSUES 1.

Whether petitioners prove that the mother of petitioner No.1 to 4 namely Smt.T.Rathnamma succumbed to the injuries sustained in the accident that took place on 08.06.2022 at about 12.30 p.m., when deceased being a pedestrian standing by the side of road, Opp to Sapthagiri Grameena Bank, Pathikonda Village, Chittoor,
Andhra Pradesh, due to the rash and negligent driving of Maruthi Swift Car bearing Regn.No.KA-05-ND-9589 by its driver?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?

sentences.text: In order to substantiate the contention of the petition, the Petitioner No.1/son of deceased got examined himself as PW.1 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.10 and closed evidence of petitioners' side.

This Tribunal answers the above issues as under:
Issue No.1: Partly in the Affirmative.
Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative.

Issue No.1:- It is the case of the petitioners that deceased succumbed to the injuries sustained in the accident that took place on 08.06.2022 at about 12.30 p.m., when the deceased was standing by the side of road, Opp to Sapthagiri Grameena Bank, Pathikonda Village, Chittoor, Andhra Pradesh,
due to the rash and negligent driving of Maruthi Swfit Car bearing Regn.No.KA-05-ND-9589 by its driver.
10. The Petitioner No.1/son of deceased Smt.T.Rathnamma examined as PW.1.
In the chief- examination, PW.1 deposed that accident occurred when his mother was standing by the side of the road, due to the rash and negligent driving of car by its driver.

In order to prove the accident and negligence of the driver of car, the petitioners produced Ex.P2 and P2(a) First Information Statement lodged by petitioner No.1/son of deceased with police on 08.06.2022.
On the basis of first information lodged by son of deceased, the police registered the case as per Ex.P.1 for the offence punishable U/s.279 & 304(A) of IPC.
In the first information statement as well as FIR, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
The petitioners furnished the sketch which is marked as Ex.P3.
The said document indicates the aspect of police visiting the place of accident after registration of FIR.
The place of accident is described in the said document and it discloses that the accident occurred by the side of the divider of the road.
Ex.P.4 & 4(a) - Inquest Report and its translated copy.
Ex. P.5 - PM report, wherein mentioned that deceased Smt.T.Rathnamma died due to head injury.
The said documents disclose the aspect of death of Rathnamma.
Ex.P.6 is the IMV Report, wherein the damages caused to vehicle are mentioned.
The said document discloses the aspect of damages caused to the vehicle and involvement of vehicle in the accident.
The driver or owner of the offending vehicle not provided satisfactory explanation regarding the manner in which damages are being caused to the vehicle.

sentences.text: In the final report also, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials to show that the investigation is not conducted in proper manner.
The final report filed by the police does not appear to have been questioned or challenged either by the driver or the owner of offending car.
11. Respondent No.3 contended that there is negligence on the part of deceased in the cause of accident.
As per the materials on record, the accident is stated to have been caused by the side of the road near the divider.
The place of accident could be depicted in Ex.P3 which discloses the place of accident.
It is the contention of respondent No.3 that the accident occurred while the deceased tried to cross the road.
The sketch furnished by the petitioners indicates the aspect of occurring of accident by the side of the divider towards North direction.
The said aspect also indicates that the deceased proceeded towards Northern side and she has crossed the divider during which time the accident appears to have been occurred.
In the cross examination, PW.1 stated that there is no zebra crossing near the place of accident and same is situated at some distance from the place of accident.
The sketch furnished before the Tribunal also does not depict the presence of zebra crossing at the place of accident.
As per the materials on record, the place of accident is a highway and there is no place provided for crossing of road for the pedestrians at the place of accident.

The accident occurred besides the divider towards the northern side which indicates that the deceased crossed the road up to the divider and at a place where no provision is made for crossing of road for the pedestrians.
On consideration of said aspects, the deceased appears to have contributed negligence towards the cause of accident.

The deceased, being pedestrian, is under the obligation to cross the road in the place provided and by crossing the road at the place where there is no provision, the deceased contributed certain amount of negligence in the cause of accident.
The quantum of negligence attributable to the deceased is 20%.
12. The oral and documentary evidence placed on record discloses the aspect of negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle as well as on the part of deceased up to certain extent.

Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of petitioners coupled with the documents produced before this tribunal, this tribunal is of the opinion that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Car bearing Regn.No.KA-05-ND- 9589 by its driver to an extent of 80% and deceased succumbed to injuries.
The deceased contributed negligence for the cause of accident to an extent of 20%.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 answered in Partly Affirmative.
13. Issue No.2:
In view of answering issue No.1 in partly affirmative, the petitioners are entitled for compensation.

In order to assess the compensation, the Tribunal has to look into several factors like age, avocation, income of deceased, conveyance charges, funeral and obsequies, towards of loss of love and affection, etc.

(A) Towards dependency and loss of future earnings:
(i) In the petition the age of the deceased Smt.T.Rathnamma, W/o.Late.T.Rajappa is shown as 57 years.
In order to prove age of deceased, the petitioners have produced Ex.P.9 - Notarized copy of Aadhaar Card of deceased, wherein her year of birth is mentioned as 1965.
The accident occurred on 08.06.2022.

The established income of the deceased was .15,500/- and 10% of .15,500/- is .1,550/-.
So, the total gross income of deceased was .15,500/- + .1,550/- = .17,050/- per month.

sentences.text: Petitioners No.1 to 4 are children of deceased.
The cause title of the petition discloses that petitioner No.1 to 4 are married.
The petitioners not furnished satisfactory materials in order to show that petitioner No.1 to 4 are dependents on the income of deceased.
Further, petitioner No.1 to 3 are the major sons of deceased which aspect could be depicted from the materials placed on record.
The petitioners not furnished satisfactory materials to show that, they were dependent on the income of deceased.
In the cross examination, PW.1 stated that he and petitioner No.2 were doing agriculture.
PW.1 also stated that petitioner No.4 is married and living in her husband's house at Panjarahalli.
On consideration of said aspects, petitioner No.1 to 4 cannot be considered to be dependent on the income of deceased.
Though the petitioners are the legal representatives of deceased, no satisfactory materials are placed before the Tribunal to show that, they are dependent on the income of deceased.
Though there is no bar for the petitioners to file petition seeking compensation but they cannot be considered to be dependents of deceased.
Though the petitioners are not entitled to compensation towards loss of dependency, they are entitled to compensation towards loss of estate.
As per the materials on record, petitioner No.1 to 4 are not considered as dependents of deceased.

As per dictum of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Smt.Sarla Verma case 50% is to be deducted from the gross income of deceased towards the personal expenses when the number of dependents is less than two and remaining is to be taken as dependency.
In the present case, as petitioner No.1 to 4 are not considered to be dependents of deceased, 50% is deducted from the gross income of deceased.

Thus petitioners are entitled to compensation of .9,20,700/- towards loss of estate which is calculated as follows:

sentences.text: 17. The petitioners filed the present petition against the respondents seeking compensation.

Respondent No.3 contended that the driver of offending car was not having valid and effective licence as on the date of accident and as such, there is violation of condition of the policy due to which respondent No.3 is not liable to pay the compensation.

Further, learned counsel for Respondent No.3 vehemently argued that after the Amendment to Motor Vehicles Act (2022) w.e.f.,
01.04.2022, no liability can be fastened on Insurance Company to pay compensation for violation of policy condition including not holding valid driving license and order for pay and recovery also cannot be passed.
The learned counsel for Respondent No.3 referred to Section 149 of the Act prior to amendment and Section 150 of the Act post Amendment.
The accident in question occurred on 08.06.2022 i.e., subsequent to the amendment which came into effect from 1/4/2022.
As per the provisions of Sec.150 of Motor Vehicles, the insurance company cannot be fastened with liability to pay compensation if there is violation of terms of the policy.

In the present case, the driver of Maruti Swift Car bearing Regn.No.KA-05-ND-9589 does not appear to have valid licence to drive the vehicle which aspect is forthcoming from the materials placed on record.

The final report filed by the jurisdictional police also discloses that the driver of Car which caused the accident, was not having valid driving license and appropriate penal provision is incorporated by the police in final report to that effect.
The materials on record disclose the aspect of violation of terms of the policy.

Though the policy pertaining to offending vehicle is in existence at the time of accident, as there is violation of terms of policy, the insurance company cannot be held liable to pay the compensation.

Further, in view of the amendment to the Act, as discussed supra, no liability can be fastened on Respondent No.3, to pay the compensation and to recover the same from the Respondent No.2 under pay and recovery theory.

18. The counsel for respondent No.3 relied on the decisions mentioned below in support of their contention:
1. MFA.No.7018 of 2023 (MV-D) C/w. MFA.No.2658 of 2024 (MV-D) in between M/s.TATA AIG Gen Ins Co Ltd.
2. MFA No.2613 of 2010 (MV) and MISC CVL 15255 of 2010 in between Smt.N.Bharathamma and others Vs. Mr.Syed Masood Matheen and another.
3. MFA No.2380 of 2016 (MV) in between Smt Gangamma Vs. Sri.Varadaraju.L and another.

sentences.text: 19. This Tribunal carefully considered the said decisions and said decisions are applicable to the case on hand.

Accordingly, the Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the liability of paying the compensation to the petitioners is to be fastened solely on the Respondent No.2, who is the owner of the offending vehicle, as he has violated the policy condition by permitting the driver of the offending vehicle to drive the same by the person having no valid driving license as on the date of the accident.
Respondent No.1 & 2 not appeared before the Tribunal in order to controvert the contention of petitioners as well as respondent No.3.
Respondent No.2 neither appeared nor placed materials to show that the vehicle involved in the accident was taken without his permission or knowledge.
Respondent No.2 not appeared before the court and also not put forth any contention contrary to the version of petitioner and respondent No.2.

No materials are placed by respondent No.2 to show that he was not having knowledge about the driver of offending vehicle not possessing driving license to drive the vehicle or aspect of not possessing the driving license was concealed from him.
Respondent No.1 neither put forth any contentions nor placed any satisfactory materials in that regard.
The final report filed by the police also indicates the aspect of driver of the offending vehicle not holding valid driving license at the time of accident.
There is violation of terms of the policy issued by respondent No.3.
As there is violation of terms of the policy, the liability cannot be fastened on respondent No.3 to pay the compensation.
Respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation.
The compensation shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
In the result Issue No.2 is answered Partly in the Affirmative.
20. Issue No.3:

In view of the findings given on the above said issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following:
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioners Under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioners are entitled for  compensation amount of .9,20,480/-
(Rupees Nine Lakhs Twenty Thousand Four Hundred and Eighty only) with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realization.
Respondent No.2, being the owner of offending vehicle, is solely liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners with interest within two months from the date of award.
This petition against the Respondent No.3 is dismissed.
Out of the total compensation amount, the petitioner No.1 to 4 being the children of deceased are entitled for equal share.
In total amount apportioned to the share of petitioner No.1 to 4, entire compensation amount shall be released in favour of petitioner No.1 to 4 as amount is meager one.

opennyai_summary.arguments:
Further the driver of alleged offending vehicle was not having driving license at the time of alleged accident.
The respondent No.1 has allowed a person who was not having valid and effective driving license to drive the same as on the date of alleged accident and as such, the respondent No.1 has violated the terms and conditions of policy.

opennyai_summary.issue:
Whether petitioners prove that the mother of petitioner No.1 to 4 namely Smt.T.Rathnamma succumbed to the injuries sustained in the accident that took place on 08.06.2022 at about 12.30 p.m., when deceased being a pedestrian standing by the side of road, Opp to Sapthagiri Grameena Bank, Pathikonda Village, Chittoor,
Andhra Pradesh, due to the rash and negligent driving of Maruthi Swift Car bearing Regn.No.KA-05-ND-9589 by its driver?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The deceased, being pedestrian, is under the obligation to cross the road in the place provided and by crossing the road at the place where there is no provision, the deceased contributed certain amount of negligence in the cause of accident.
The quantum of negligence attributable to the deceased is 20%.
12. The oral and documentary evidence placed on record discloses the aspect of negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle as well as on the part of deceased up to certain extent.
In the absence of rebuttal materials, the document furnished by petitioners is to be taken for consideration for ascertaining the age of deceased.
As per the materials on record, the age of deceased was 57 years as on the date of accident and same is taken into consideration.
In the absence of satisfactory materials, notional income of deceased is to be considered.
Tummisi Gangulappa vs Kaju Eswara Raju on 10 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163952893/
6
Though there is no bar for the petitioners to file petition seeking compensation but they cannot be considered to be dependents of deceased.
Though the petitioners are not entitled to compensation towards loss of dependency, they are entitled to compensation towards loss of estate.
As per the provisions of Sec.150 of Motor Vehicles, the insurance company cannot be fastened with liability to pay compensation if there is violation of terms of the policy.
In the present case, the driver of Maruti Swift Car bearing Regn.No.KA-05-ND-9589 does not appear to have valid licence to drive the vehicle which aspect is forthcoming from the materials placed on record.
The final report filed by the jurisdictional police also discloses that the driver of Car which caused the accident, was not having valid driving license and appropriate penal provision is incorporated by the police in final report to that effect.
Though the policy pertaining to offending vehicle is in existence at the time of accident, as there is violation of terms of policy, the insurance company cannot be held liable to pay the compensation.
Further, in view of the amendment to the Act, as discussed supra, no liability can be fastened on Respondent No.3, to pay the compensation and to recover the same from the Respondent No.2 under pay and recovery theory.
Accordingly, the Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the liability of paying the compensation to the petitioners is to be fastened solely on the Respondent No.2, who is the owner of the offending vehicle, as he has violated the policy condition by permitting the driver of the offending vehicle to drive the same by the person having no valid driving license as on the date of the accident.
Respondent No.2 neither appeared nor placed materials to show that the vehicle involved in the accident was taken without his permission or knowledge.
No materials are placed by respondent No.2 to show that he was not having knowledge about the driver of offending vehicle not possessing driving license to drive the vehicle or aspect of not possessing the driving license was concealed from him.
The final report filed by the police also indicates the aspect of driver of the offending vehicle not holding valid driving license at the time of accident.
As there is violation of terms of the policy, the liability cannot be fastened on respondent No.3 to pay the compensation.
